author: (unsigned; SDA Year Book 1889)
text: XVIII. That as all have violated the law of God, and cannot of themselves render obedience to his just requirements, we are dependent on Christ, first, for justification from our past offenses, and, secondly, for grace whereby to render acceptable obedience to his holy law in time to come.
note: The 1889 anchor: Christ gives two things, justification for past sins and then grace to obey his law.

author: A. T. Jones
work: The Great Nations of To-day (the same paragraph ran in the unsigned editorial “The Third Angel’s Message. The Faith of Jesus,” Review and Herald 77, no. 43, Oct. 23, 1900, pp. 680–681 = ARSH October 23,  1900, page 680.16)
text: In Christ, by faith of Christ, the believer in Jesus finds the keeping of the commandments of God, which is the righteousness of God. Thus the keeping of the commandments of God is the gift of God: it is the “free gift” of the righteousness of God “which is by faith of Jesus Christ unto all and upon all them that believe.” And this is the Third Angel’s Message: “Here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.”
note: Jones: keeping the commandments is itself God's gift received by faith, and that is the third angel's message of Rev 14:12.

author: E. J. Waggoner
work: “Studies in the Book of Hebrews. - No. 16” (Sunday afternoon, Feb. 28, 1897), General Conference Daily Bulletin, March 8, 1897 (byline at page 297; the corpus author field names the editor, A. T. Jones)
text: But I think anybody here can see that the third angel’s message is righteousness by faith; for the Sabbath is righteousness by faith; for by it a man comes into God’s works, and those works are perfect. Therefore he gets rest by faith. … If he does not believe God, then he cannot keep the Sabbath.
note: Waggoner: keeping the fourth commandment is itself righteousness by faith, and so is the third angel's message.

author: Ellen G. White
work: Letter 57, 1895 (to O. A. Olsen, May 1, 1895, per the 1888 Materials index); printed as TM 92.1
text: The uplifted Saviour is to appear in His efficacious work as the Lamb slain, sitting upon the throne to dispense the priceless covenant blessings, the benefits He died to purchase for every soul who should believe on Him. … Christ is pleading for the church in the heavenly courts above, pleading for those for whom He paid the redemption price of His own life blood. Centuries, ages, can never diminish the efficacy of this atoning sacrifice. This message of the gospel of His grace was to be given to the church in clear and distinct lines, that the world should no longer say, Seventh-day Adventists talk the law, the law, but do not preach or believe Christ.
note: The paragraph right after the 'most precious message' paragraph (par. 43): the 1888 message sets forth Christ pleading now in the heavenly courts.

author: Ellen G. White
work: Testimonies for the Church, vol. 5, ch. 53 “Joshua and the Angel” (first printed 1885 as T32 228.2)
text: Zechariah’s vision of Joshua and the Angel applies with peculiar force to the experience of God’s people in the closing up of the great day of atonement. The remnant church will be brought into great trial and distress. Those who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus will feel the ire of the dragon and his hosts.
note: EGW sets the filthy-garments vision in the closing up of the great day of atonement, when commandment-keepers feel the dragon's ire.

author: A. T. Jones
work: The Consecrated Way to Christian Perfection, ch. XVI “The Times of Refreshing”
text: … we know by every evidence that now we are in the times of refreshing—the time of the latter rain. And as certainly as that is so, we are also in the time of the utter blotting out of all sins that have ever been against us. And the blotting out of sins is exactly this thing of the cleansing of the sanctuary; it is the finishing of all transgression in our lives; it is the making an end of all sins in our character; it is the bringing in of the very righteousness of God which is by faith of Jesus Christ, to abide alone everlastingly.
note: Jones ties righteousness by faith to the latter rain, the blotting out of sins and the cleansing of the sanctuary.
